articles.title: Kate Beckinsale Posts Cryptic Messages on Social Media, Sparking Concern from Fans
articles.summary: “Serendipity” actor Kate Beckinsale posted cryptic messages to her personal social media account early Sunday morning, leaving fans concerned. Beckinsale posted a black screen with “bye” written across it on her Instagram story, followed by a second post of a rainbow with the text “congratulations…
body: The actress has a history of taking to social media to air her grievances. In a since-deleted Instagram video from earlier in September, Beckinsale said that “people have seen or experienced levels of horror, terror, violence” don’t “just dream about incessantly, so there’s no rest. They see it when they blink. Every time they close their eyes for a second and those people aren’t recognized as heroes.”

“Given the fact that it’s invisible and you can’t know, maybe err on being on the gentler side with people, being kinder with people,” she added at the time. “It really is true that if you haven’t walked a mile in someone’s shoes — however fancy you feel the shoes are — you have absolutely no idea what they may be carrying or masking or dealing with day and night.”

After her mother Judy Loe’s death in July 2025 after a battle with stage IV cancer, Beckinsale discussed her struggles online. People reported that she previously shared on her Instagram dozens of negative comments she’s received about her appearance amid her grief.

articles.title: Sylvester Stallone Says He Turned Down Trump’s ‘Special Ambassador’ to Hollywood Role Because It Was ‘Impossible’: ‘I Said Thank You and Ciao’
articles.summary: Sylvester Stallone may hold the Trump-bestowed title of “special ambassador” to Hollywood, but nearly two years since his appointment, the “Rocky” actor has divulged that he didn’t explicitly sign up for the role.
body: He even recalled telling Trump that “it won’t work.” “I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible. Hollywood works, and it will evolve. It’s corporate and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance.”

Despite Stallone’s initial feelings about the appointment, the actor still speaks fondly of Trump. In the interview, Stallone noted that he introduced the president-elect as a “mythical character” when at a party at Mar-a-Lago. “Nobody in the world could’ve pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe,” he said.

articles.title: NFL’s 20 Hottest WAGs: Taylor Swift, Madison Beer, Normani and More
articles.summary: The term WAGs (wives and girlfriends) was popularized by the U.K. press in the early aughts in relation to Victoria Beckham, a pop singer for the Spice Girls who was married to star footballer David Beckham and a frequent fixture at his matches.
body: A term previously used to describe the wives of girlfriends of footballers across the pond has traveled to America’s most popular sport.

The coupling of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce, the pop superstar and stud tight end for the NFL’s Kansas City Chiefs (who now makes considerable more money off the field via his podcast and brand deals), has put the NFL’s WAGs under the spotlight. Swift almost single-handedly increased the NFL’s popularity among girls and women, including a 53% increase among girls aged 12-17 and 34% increase in women 35+, while adding an estimated $1 billion+ in revenue to the league.

And the NFL took notice. Prior to this season, the league highlighted its WAGs like pop star Madison Beer (fiancée of Chargers QB Justin Herbert), model Olivia Ponton (girlfriend of Bengals QB Joe Burrow) and influencer Marissa Ayers (Giants QB Jaxson Dart’s partner) by capturing footage of them getting cozy with their significant others at NFL training camp as part of a coordinated content rollout.

articles.title: From Oprah Winfrey and Christopher Nolan to Kim Kardashian and Robert De Niro: Inside the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art Opening Gala
articles.summary: During her introductory remarks at the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art on Saturday night, Mellody Hobson said her husband, famed “Star Wars” director George Lucas, was nervous about the evening’s turnout. “This room is filled with our friends,” Hobson said.
body: Lucas said he wanted to create a cultural institution that honors illustrators. “When we started this museum, we would sort of tag it as a ‘temple to illustrators,’” he said.

While Winfrey, Erivo, Kardashian and Rodriguez strolled through the galleries, most of the heavy hitters made their way to the fifth-floor Skywalker Grill restaurant. DiCaprio enjoyed sushi in a banquette with Al Pacino, Andrew Watt and David Furnish. Nolan bent over to say hello to a seated Coppola. Ron Howard and his daughter Bryce Dallas Howard took photos with Kardashian and her boyfriend, car racing champion Lewis Hamilton.

Building the $1.5 billion museum, which was entirely funded by Lucas and Hobson, came with plenty of headaches. In the 20 years since Lucas first proposed the idea, the museum was close to being located in San Francisco and then Chicago. Located in L.A.’s Exposition Park, the Lucas Museum features 1,200 works from Lucas’s 30,000-piece private art collection. Designed by Ma Yansong of MAD Architects, the five-story building, which is frequently described as a “spaceship,” is 300,000 square feet, with 100,000 dedicated to 35 galleries, and sits among a 13-acre campus.

articles.title: ‘Resident Evil movies? I’ve never seen one’: Weapons director Zach Cregger on resurrecting the beloved zombie franchise
articles.summary: Raised on punk, alt-comedy and the church, Cregger’s Lynchian approach to horror is anything but typical. After two wildly original hits, his pivot to a 30-year-old video game has caused a storm among protective fans.
body: Even if Cregger had not had a box-office smash that crossed over into awards contention, there would still be an atmosphere of hushed expectation around his next move. Both Barbarian and Weapons addressed hot-button issues – sexual assault and school shootings, respectively – while resisting easy interpretation. Both, too, started out seemingly heading in one narrative direction, before thrillingly careening off elsewhere. Thus, with just two features, Cregger had established a reputation for totally terrifying, utterly unpredictable and – most importantly – genuinely original movies.

Yet the real shocker from this nascent horror auteur is still to come. For his third film, Cregger has taken inspiration from existing intellectual property – or IP, those two little letters bound to strike fear into the heart of even the most stoic cineaste. Zach Cregger has made a Resident Evil movie.

articles.title: Strictly returns with new hosting trio as celebrities find out dance pairings
articles.summary: Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Radebe take over from long-running presenting duo Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman.
body: Strictly Come Dancing has returned to the small screen for its 24th series, in a new era for the show with a revamped presenting line-up.
An average of 5.3 million viewers tuned in on Saturday with a share of 49.2% of the overnight ratings, which was 7% up on last year, and it remained high on iPlayer's most popular chart on Sunday.
Broadcaster Emma Willis, comedian Josh Widdicombe and former Strictly professional Johannes Radebe made their presenting debut, taking over from Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman, who left last year.
Famous faces including actress Melanie Walters and former England footballer Shaun Wright-Phillips stepped on to the ballroom floor for the first time.

articles.title: Charlize Theron Says ‘The Odyssey’ Just Gave Hollywood a Much-Needed Reminder
articles.summary: The star, who played Calypso in Christopher Nolan's box office smash, continued her busy year as she hosted the annual benefit for her Charlize Theron Africa Outreach Project.
body: Nearly 20 years after founding CTAOP, the Oscar-winning actress reflected on its impact, which has helped close to 5 million people across South Africa – and on the overwhelming response to Christopher Nolan ’s The Odyssey and what it could signal for Hollywood going forward.

“It’s so rewarding to see that people do want to go to the theaters,” Theron told The Hollywood Reporter at the event. “They do want to go and see movies, and if we were ever questioning it, we shouldn’t anymore.”

Theron, who plays Calypso in Nolan’s epic, said the response has been particularly encouraging at a time when the industry remains uncertain about the future of moviegoing. “I do think my industry is really worried about where we are going and what’s happening,” she said. “I think we needed a little bit of this reminder that people do love to watch movies in the theater.”

articles.title: Before Star Trek, William Shatner Appeared In A Cinematic Adaptation Of A Beloved Book
articles.summary: William Shatner's role in this film adaptation of a highly-esteemed book helped him break out prior to being cast in Star Trek: The Original Series.
body: There was a time in William Shatner's career, when he was still an up-and-coming young buck, that he had a propensity for the classics. At the very least, he starred in a few impressive cinematic adaptations of important Western Canon titles. One of Shatner's very first and best non-"Star Trek" projects, for instance, was Tyrone Guthrie's 1957 filmed production of Sophocles' "Oedipus Rex" (in which Shatner plays a member of the masked chorus). The script for that film was taken from William Butler Yeats' adaptation, so it possesses a modern sense of English poetry. It's a pretty great movie.

Some trivia books may refer to Brooks' "The Brothers Karamazov" as Shatner's film debut, but that's not entirely accurate. It would be more correct to say that it marked Shatner's first notable leading cinematic role. He was only about 26 or 27 during production and projected the requisite innocence. He has always been a very assured performer, even if he often gets grief for his sometimes-halting line delivery ( although Shatner has a reason for speaking that way ).

articles.title: From OnlyFans to San Sebastian: How Gina Jaqueline Brought Unsettling Authenticity to Her Debut Acting Role in ‘Cute’
articles.summary: Marlene Emilie Lyngstad is open to the idea that her first feature film, following a man attracted to his seven-year-old stepdaughter, could prompt walk-outs: "I just want people to think about all the questions that he brings to the table."
body: When Marlene Emilie Lyngstad hosted San Sebastian Film Festival director José Luis Rebordinos for a screening of her debut feature, Cute, she was admittedly extremely nervous.

The Nordisk Film Production is, indeed, as dicey as it sounds: Røise’s character clings to the stepchild’s frilly, pink sock as he sleeps, pleasures himself to her voice, and enjoys infantilizing Stella by feeding her dinner and brushing her teeth.

So, during the years-long development of this film, Lyngstad searched far and wide for actors who could do such a sensitive “hot topic” justice. In Gina Jaqueline, an OnlyFans creator and social media influencer — and who has so much in common with Stella that she couldn’t believe Lyngstad was unaware of her previous work — the character was brought to life with, to the director’s delight, unnerving authenticity.

articles.title: Charlie Hunnam Officially Reveals His Biggest Fear Filming ‘Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story’ (And It’s Not What You Think)
articles.summary: Charlie Hunnam reveals his biggest fear while filming Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story and breaks down Bridget and Andrew’s complex relationship.
body: Taylor Gates is an Indiana native who earned her BFA in Creative Writing from the University of Evansville. She fell in love with entertainment by watching shows about chaotic families like Full House, The Nanny, Gilmore Girls, and The Fosters. After college, she moved to Los Angeles to pursue a career as a writer, editor, and filmmaker. Today, she’s a sucker for dramedies — especially coming-of-age stories centering around complex female and LGBTQ+ characters. She has been with Collider since May 2022.
This interview contains spoilers for the first two episodes of Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.

Charlie Hunnam has had a long and diverse career. Though best known for playing Jax Teller in the motorcycle club crime drama Sons of Anarchy, his television resume also includes Queer as Folk and cult favorite Undeclared, with notable film roles including action-adventure films Triple Frontier and King Arthur: Legend of the Sword. He most recently starred as famous serial killer Ed Gein in the last installment of Monster, for which he was nominated for his first Emmy.

articles.title: Inside the Star-Studded Opening Night of the Lucas Museum: “A New Institution Is Being Born”
articles.summary: George Lucas and Mellody Hobson celebrated their new L.A. museum with the help of Harrison Ford, Leonardo DiCaprio, Oprah, Steven Spielberg, Christopher Nolan, Kim Kardashian and many more.
body: Before the new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens to the public on Tuesday, George Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, threw an opening night celebration that will go down in the Hollywood history books.

Queen Latifah, a close friend of the couple, opened the evening as she told the crowd of stars, “Nobody gets to go to a night like this. No one was in the room when the doors opened at the MoMA, or at the Louvre in 1793, or the Met… so we’ve got to feel the gravity of this moment because this is enormous. When you look around, your inclination may be to catch up with friends tonight; we’re all artists in awe of each other, but I implore you to soak this in. Allow these artists to speak to you.”

Architect Ma Yansong spoke briefly before Hobson took the stage, as she teased, “If your husband or spouse comes home and says they want to build a museum, I suggest your response is a hard no.” She explained, “I used to joke with George that at home, one of my jobs as his wife was to serve as a pair of gravity boots; I’d say, ‘George, stay with us,’ as I tried to hold him down. But this time, he pulled me up with him.”
